Nodes.Text: The moss keeps its own time out here. Sit, if you're weary — the fire takes eight drams and asks no questions.

Choices.Text: What grows down in the caves?

Nodes.Text: Quartz that hums, down past the sandstone. Miners cracked veins of it before the snapjaws took the shafts back. Bring a strong arm; the veins give to anyone patient.
You walk loud for someone so far from water. Rest is eight drams. The dunes will still be here after.

Choices.Text: What should I fear out here?

Nodes.Text: The sand moves where nothing walks — wurms below, and worse things sleeping in the old tombs. The bandits dig little dens and think the desert doesn't notice. It notices.
Hold still. You've been walking through my garden and half of it walks back. If something bit you, I can draw it out — no charge; the Rotwood poisons enough on its own. A proper rest is eight drams.

Choices.Text: What's safe to eat out there?

Nodes.Text: Mendleaf, if you find it before the rotlings do. Never the pale caps. And if the choir's tendrils start humming at you — walk away slow. They remember faces.
Mind the rubble. The lamp stays lit so the old streets remember someone still walks them. Eight drams buys you a rest in its circle.

Libraries, mostly collapsed. Shelves still holding books nobody living can price. The brass husks patrol like the city never fell — and the cultists scratch their runes where the old words used to be. Both will kill you; only one will mean it.
